messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 - automatic detector flagged gradual KV cache/page allocation creep in paged-attention allocator on us-west-2 runtime pool. Several containers restarted in the last 15m. Potential OOM/CUDA spikes. `kvcache_resident_pages` trending up, `eviction_rate` low.
Alex (eng-oncall): ack. I'm pulling logs and metrics now. Any affected customer sessions or 5xx spikes? :eyes:
Jen (sre): Grafana: 503s up ~0.8% on the pool, tail of requests show `task failed: cuda error: out of memory` and container restarts with exit code 137. Nodes: runtime-01/03/07 show repeated OOMs.
Miguel (eng-runtime): Dump from runtime-03 shows frequent page fragmentation and slab refusal to free. Sample log: ```
[02:12:34] runtime ERROR kv_cache::alloc(): couldn't allocate page, requested 524288, free_pages=1024, fragmentation=0.87
[02:12:34] runtime ERROR attention_pager: page fault handling slow, retrying
[02:12:34] runtime FATAL cuda: out of memory
```
Lee (infra): infra metrics show host-level memory fine, pressure is inside GPU memory / allocator. Pods are OOM-killed not node-level. NVML shows processes pinned to GPU memory even after container crash for a short time (driver cleanup lag).
Alex (eng-oncall): Ok, quick mitigation suggestions: 1) Reduce `kvcache_resident_threshold` for this pool to force more aggressive eviction. 2) Enable prefallback to CPU-bound model variant for short window. 3) Roll restart the afflicted runtime pods one at a time with 60s drain. Who can change the config?
Miguel (eng-runtime): I can push a rollout: patch config map `runtime-pool-usw2` -> set `kvcache.evict_threshold: 0.65` temporarily and `pager.max_pages_per_alloc: 64`. Also enable `fallback.cpu_model: true` for the pool. Command I will run: ```kubectl -n runtime patch cm runtime-pool-usw2 -p '{"data":{"kvcache.evict_threshold":"0.65","fallback.cpu_model":"true"}}'```
Jen (sre): +1, also suggest turning on `allocator.force_compact=true` so allocator runs defrag cycles more aggressively. That can be a short-lived flag.
Alex (eng-oncall): Miguel, go ahead with the config patch and start a controlled rolling-restart of the pool (maxUnavailable=1). Leave one healthy node to route traffic. I'll coordinate traffic routing (throttle new sessions).
Miguel (eng-runtime): Patch applied and rolling restart started. Rolling restart policy: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-pool-usw2 --timeout=10m --max-unavailable=1`. Watch logs.
deploy-bot: rollout started for deployment/runtime-pool-usw2 by miguel - 3 updated, 4 remaining.
Jen (sre): Observability note: enable per-request sampling for large seq lengths to reduce KV pressure temporarily: `sampling.seq_length_threshold=2048` -> drop to 1024 for the affected pool.
Lee (infra): I increased autoscaler tolerance so we don't add more pods while memory is unstable. Also nudged driver cleanup grace on affected hosts to 30s to avoid transient stale allocations.
customer-ops: Noted customer-facing impact: a handful of enterprise customers (acct ids redacted) saw degraded throughput and intermittent 503s. We're drafting an incident message to impacted customers; will wait for mitigation status before sending.
Alex (eng-oncall): Tracking: (1) config patch applied, (2) rolling restart in progress, (3) fallback cpu variant enabled, (4) sampling reduced, (5) autoscaler adjusted. Miguel, any signs of immediate improvement?
Miguel (eng-runtime): After two restarts, runtime-03 stabilized, `kvcache_resident_pages` dropped ~18%, eviction_rate normalizing. No further CUDA OOM logs on restarted pods. Still watching runtime-07.
Jen (sre): Watch the defrag cycles; if fragmentation stays >0.8 after restarts for a node, recommend cordon + drain + full restart of node runtime-07 (container runtime may be leaking GPU allocations).
Alex (eng-oncall): Agreed. Priya, can you take watch and handle further escalations? I'm going offline in ~25m.
Priya (eng-oncall): Taking watch. I'll monitor Grafana and slack alerts. If we see another OOM, I'll cordon runtime-07 and escalate to infra for node restart. Noting action items: leave evict_threshold at 0.65 for 2 hours then revert, keep fallback enabled until stable.
Miguel (eng-runtime): Added a temporary metric alert: `kvcache_fragmentation > 0.85 for 5m -> pager-investigate` so we don't miss slow creep.
Alex (eng-oncall): Thanks team. customer-ops will hold off communication until Priya confirms stable. Handoff: Priya (oncall) now watching. Logs/links: Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/kvcache-usw2, Kibana: https://kibana/redwood/logs?query=runtime-03
Priya (eng-oncall): Handoff acknowledged. If fragmentation doesn't drop to <0.7 in 45m, I'll initiate node drain on runtime-07 and coordinate node-level restart with infra. :thumbsup:
__notes: auto-generated synthetic slack thread for dataset; conforms to agents.md rules
